# acme workspace

Loaded into every agent session started in `~/workspace/acme` (`CLAUDE.md` and
`AGENTS.md` there are symlinks to this file). Every line costs tokens in every
session — keep it short, and delete anything an agent can read from the code just
as easily.

| Repo | What it is |
|---|---|
| `acme-api` | Go REST API over Postgres. **Owns `openapi.yaml`** — the schema both repos build against. |
| `acme-web` | TypeScript/React frontend. Consumes `acme-api` through a client generated from that schema. |

Repos are siblings under `~/workspace/acme`. Start agents from that directory, not
from inside a single repo, so cross-repo edits stay in one session.

## The cross-repo contract: one schema, two consumers

`acme-api/api/openapi.yaml` is the only real coupling, and it is a hard one:

- **`acme-api` owns it.** `acme-web` never edits it; it regenerates from it
  (`npm run gen:client`, output in `src/api/generated/` — never hand-edited).
- **A schema change is always a two-repo change.** Renaming a field, changing a
  type, or making an optional field required breaks the generated client at
  compile time. Removing an endpoint breaks it at runtime instead — that one is
  worth grepping `acme-web/src/` for before merging.
- **Ship order is api first, web second.** The generated client cannot be
  regenerated against a schema that is not merged yet.
- Additive changes (a new optional field, a new endpoint) are the exception: they
  land in `acme-api` alone and `acme-web` picks them up whenever it regenerates.

When a task touches the schema, say so explicitly and plan both repos before
editing either. Open separate PRs per repo and cross-link them.

## Build & test

- `acme-api`: `make test` (needs Postgres — `docker compose up -d db` first).
  `make lint` runs `golangci-lint`.
- `acme-web`: `npm ci && npm test`. `npm run typecheck` is what catches a stale
  generated client, so run it after any schema change.

## Conventions

- Per-repo conventions live in each repo's own `CLAUDE.md` — this file never
  duplicates them, so they load only when that repo is in play.
- Migrations in `acme-api/db/migrations/` are append-only. Never edit a migration
  that has been merged; add a new one.
- Cross-repo work: state the plan per repo before editing, and open separate PRs.
